question.problem: At a call center, the time taken for phone calls to be answered varies continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of $3$ calls every minute. What is the probability of taking more than $1$ minute to answer the next call? Round your answer to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Since the time until the next call is answered occurs continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next call is answered using an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ be the time, in minutes, between calls. Then, since there are $3$ calls per minute on average, the rate is $\lambda =3$ calls per minute.

The amount of time before the next call can be modeled as an exponential random variable with rate $\lambda =3,$ and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(3).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}3{e}^{-3x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the next call will occur after $1$ minute or more is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 1) & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }3{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-3x}{|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =-{e}^{-\infty }+{e}^{-3} \\  & =0+{e}^{-3} \\  & ={e}^{-3} \\  & ≈0.0498.\end{aligned}
$$
